posts.name: WriterRyan
posts.cooked:
I can’t say for sure about how much Multiverse-ness will come into play. However, TheJayMann is right (maybe?).

It kind of depends on how you want to look at time travel.
If things were to proceed without The Visionary coming back in time, they would happen as they have already done so in her past. However, now she has come back in time to stop those events from happening.

One school of time travel, which doesn’t make so much sense, would have her altering her own universe. The problem with this is that then there’s no reason for her to travel back through time to alter it. This time travel idea is a little brighter because it posits that one could fix the past, but like I said, it doesn’t make much sense this way.

The second school of time travel suggests that every time someone alters the past a new universe branches off. I don’t know if anyone here reads it, but Dr. McNinja has been dealing with this concept lately.
